At the gate

Less time at the sign-up table.

At the sign-up table, type the driver's name into RaceDay on your check-in device — or tap it if they've raced with you before — and pick their classes. Their heat pill draws automatically, usually in under 15 seconds. You're still collecting waivers and entry fees at the table — RaceDay just skips the handwritten roster.

Heats build themselves the moment sign-up closes: pill order, inside/outside lines, B-mains and features, all laid out and ready to post before the drivers' meeting.

Plug any TV into the wall. RaceDay fills the screen with rotating lineups — no crowding the tower to read a printout.
After the checkers

Enter finishes. Points update themselves.

Tap the cars in the order they finish — or use the number pad, or import a CSV straight from your timing system. Standings, the B-main, and the feature lineup all build from those numbers automatically.

Season points update the instant a feature is scored. No Monday-morning spreadsheet, no re-adding a season by hand.

Everything else

Organized, not just fast.

A driver book that remembers every racer year to year. Backups you can export anytime. A full audit trail of every result edit. Race-day history you can pull up months later.

Runs in a browser on whatever laptop or tablet you already own — nothing to install, nothing to configure on a server.

For the fans in the stands

Not just who's winning.

The same free link fans already use for live lineups also opens up context most racing software skips entirely: tap a class to see what it's about, tap any driver's name mid-lineup for their stats, hometown, and sponsors.

Most of what's out there stops at a name and a lap time. RaceDay's built so a stranger in the stands — or on their couch, watching the same link — understands what they're looking at, not just who's ahead.

Introducing DrivenNow live

One profile.
Every track you race.

Drivers build a free Driven profile once — name, car number, photo, sponsors — and it follows them to every track running RaceDay. At sign-up they hand over a short link code instead of retyping everything, and the track sends their results straight back.

Every driver gets a public page to share with fans and sponsors — latest result, starts, wins, top 5s and average finish, with every result posted by the track's own scoring, never typed in. Pro ($3/mo or $30/yr) adds the full broadcast look: a header photo, three team colors, points standings, season form and milestone badges.

Why it's free to try

I built RaceDay because I wanted a race night to run off a laptop instead of a clipboard.

It's new for this season, so I'm not going to pretend a dozen tracks are already running it — you'd be one of the first. What that means for you: every class gets set up by hand with you, and I'm reachable on your first race night if something doesn't behave.

Free trial, no card, no pressure. If it earns its keep, we'll talk about a license that costs less than one night's gate.
